assumptions: commensurate finite-dimensional linear system in Matignon framework

assumptions: System admits the recursive closed-loop representation used by the authors.

assumptions: Lyapunov/comparison hypotheses of source

notes: Promising starting point for structured subclass follow-up.

assumptions: Common-matrix/quadratic stability interpretation

assumptions: Specific diffusive predator-prey Double-Allee model
statement_summary: Provides analytical coexistence/stability and pattern-formation/bifurcation conditions for the source model.

assumptions: Specific predator-prey model with Double-Allee prey term
statement_summary: Uses fractional spectral criteria and Lyapunov analysis to derive local/global conditions and order/parameter-driven oscillatory behavior.

notes: Recent direct prior art.

assumptions: Discrete fractional predator-prey model and parameter restrictions of source

notes: Direct falsification of discrete-fractional novelty.

assumptions: Real matrices of dimensions 2, 3 or 4 under source sign convention

notes: Exact finite structural prior art.

notes: Complexity evidence; do not upgrade wording to formal NP-completeness.

assumptions: Metzler matrix and lower-dimensional construction of source
statement_summary: Hurwitz stability of a Metzler matrix can be tested via signs of diagonal entries of recursively constructed lower-dimensional matrices; source uses fact Hurwitz Metzler is diagonally stable.
limitations: Ordinary Hurwitz region; prescribed conic angular margin remains separate.
notes: Shows positive/Metzler ordinary D-stability is highly constrained.

assumptions: Specific two-component single-species model of source
statement_summary: Deterministic equilibria existence/stability are rigorously analyzed; stochastic R0^s is a sharp extinction/permanence threshold.
limitations: Publisher abstract does not establish a general component-function composition theorem.
notes: Strongest direct prior result against C-DA-1 in this round.

assumptions: Prey regulation and predator size-selection assumptions of source
statement_summary: Emergent predator Allee effects occur only under specified juvenile-stage density regulation/overcompensatory maturation and depend on size-selective predation.
limitations: Not a two separable component-deletion theorem.
notes: Shows emergent threshold theorems exist outside Double-Allee vocabulary.

network_structure: connected undirected graph; generalized graph Laplacian
assumptions: Source condition (S), migration survival p, diffusion d, connected undirected graph
statement_summary: There is a monotone threshold relation in diffusion/migration separating uniform persistence from local extinction, with cases determined by aggregate growth and graph/migration parameters.
limitations: Local reaction can be logistic or bistable but internal component decomposition is not retained.
notes: Strongest theorem against generic C-DA-2.

assumptions: Individual component effect and aggregation/spatial assumptions of source
statement_summary: Endogenous spatial structure controls whether an individual-level component Allee effect manifests as a demographic Allee effect; threshold/group-level conditions are derived in the source framework.
limitations: One principal component mechanism; not double dormancy composition of two components.
notes: Strong conceptual threat to overly broad C-DA-1.

assumptions: Network/subsystem model class and input-output assumptions of source
statement_summary: Network is structurally identifiable iff all subsystems are identifiable; graph-hierarchical decomposition partitions the network into identifiable subsystems.
limitations: Not an ecological Allee model and not continuous-time Caputo threshold inference.
notes: Blocks generic novelty claim for fractional-network structural identifiability.

assumptions: Known input/output frequency contents and source model set
statement_summary: Both structural/model and parameter identifiability decrease markedly for smaller fractional order even with rich inputs.
limitations: Controlled-input setting; not passive ecology.
notes: Relevant obstruction for adding fractional memory.

theorem_label: low-abundance data necessity for practical Allee inference
assumptions: Atlantic herring stock-recruitment data and source model set
statement_summary: Removing low-abundance observations makes evidence for depensation/Allee effects weaken and uncertainty expand; high-abundance data cannot objectively discriminate low-abundance dynamics.
limitations: Not structural identifiability theorem; aggregate demographic data.
notes: Critical design constraint for C-DA-3.

theorem_label: multi-stage density regulation can generate alternative stable states
assumptions: Specified exponential/linear/hyperbolic density-dependence combinations of source
statement_summary: For the exponential survival + exponential fecundity case, sufficiently large intrinsic growth can yield up to three equilibrium population sizes, two stable.
limitations: Parametric life-stage model; no component-deletion double-dormancy theorem.
notes: Direct historical threat to broad novelty of multiplicative vital-rate composition.

theorem_label: countervailing vital-rate density dependence removes Allee effect
assumptions: Piriqueta projection matrix parameterized from experiments and demographic study
statement_summary: Including only positive density dependence in fecundity gives an Allee effect; including increased low-density survival removes it because survival has greater population-growth elasticity.
limitations: Species-specific empirical model; no general necessary/sufficient composition theorem.
notes: Shows component deletion/counterfactual combinations are established ecological practice.

assumptions: Tribolium experimental design and fitted density-dependent fecundity/survival functions
statement_summary: Population growth density dependence is modeled as the product of density-dependent fecundity and survival; both components are experimentally estimated.
limitations: Not an Allee-threshold composition theorem.
notes: Direct prior art for multiplicative component-fitness architecture.

theorem_label: two interacting Allee effects survival/extinction scenarios
matrix_structure: mate-finding + predation Allee effects with reproduction/predation trade-off
assumptions: Specific trade-off shapes and component mechanisms of source
statement_summary: Source distinguishes qualitative survival/extinction scenarios generated by simultaneous reproductive and predation Allee effects and their trade-off.
limitations: Trade-off/model-specific, not general component-function deletion theorem.
notes: Mandatory ROUND-0006 prior threat.

theorem_label: observation-preserving Lie symmetries characterize structural non-identifiability transformations
assumptions: Coupled differential-equation model and specified observation function
statement_summary: The local Lie algebra of model symmetries is constructed; the subalgebra preserving the observation gives transformations that preserve observed model structure, equivalent to the similarity-transformation approach for structural-identifiability analysis.
limitations: Finite-dimensional state/parameter setting in source; frozen A_i are unrestricted functions.
notes: Strongest conceptual killer of standalone gauge-symmetry novelty.

assumptions: Model/algorithm conditions of source
statement_summary: A set of algebraically independent identifiable parameter combinations can be found, and the input-output equations admit a unique rational reparameterization over those combinations under the stated framework.
limitations: Finite-dimensional parameters; does not directly cover unrestricted unknown functions.
notes: Product-only identifiable combinations are standard structural-ID objects.

theorem_label: minimal output sets ensuring structural identifiability
matrix_structure: parametric dynamic models with selectable outputs
assumptions: Specified model and candidate measurable outputs
statement_summary: Iterative structural-identifiability analysis can determine minimal sets of measured outputs whose inclusion renders model parameters structurally identifiable.
limitations: Algorithmic/general parametric setting; not a closed-form ecology-specific m-factor theorem.
notes: Strongest generic killer of standalone minimal-output novelty.

assumptions: Biological dynamic models satisfying source method assumptions
statement_summary: Model symmetries causing structural unidentifiability/unobservability can be detected; symmetry-breaking transformations or reparameterizations can restore an observable/identifiable representation.
limitations: Parametric dynamic-system focus; no ecology-specific functional product decomposition.
notes: Confirms product gauge belongs to established symmetry framework.

theorem_label: output invariance equals structural unidentifiability under original dynamical-compensation definition
assumptions: Original dynamical-compensation definition and observation setting of source
statement_summary: If varying a parameter leaves the observed output trajectory unchanged for all admissible inputs in the original DC1 sense, that property is structural unidentifiability with respect to that output.
limitations: Parameter rather than unknown-function gauge.
notes: Strong biological precedent for interpreting invariance as non-identifiability.

assumptions: Identical-patch strong-Allee model with common threshold beta and dispersal alpha under source graph assumptions
statement_summary: For complete digraphs bifurcation polynomials are derived for all n>1; equilibrium counts are completely classified for n<=14, and for fixed n with alpha>=3/n only three steady states remain.
limitations: Generic strong-Allee network; no hidden component-factor identifiability.
notes: Additional network novelty threat only.

dimension: finite decision dimension / infinite constraint index
assumptions: Linear inequalities indexed by arbitrary/infinite set
statement_summary: The feasible set of a linear semi-infinite program is the intersection of its constraint halfspaces and is therefore convex; under closed constraints it is closed.
limitations: Generic optimization fact; no Allee-specific biological phase interpretation.
notes: Subsumes novelty of P2 half-space/convexity claims.

assumptions: Regularity assumptions of Danskin theorem; unique maximizer for simple gradient form
statement_summary: For a value function defined as a maximum over an inner variable, at a unique maximizer the derivative with respect to parameters equals the parameter derivative of the inner objective evaluated at that maximizer.
limitations: Requires regularity/uniqueness for classical differentiable form.
notes: Directly subsumes P5 formula ∇M=-g(x*).

theorem_label: minimal winning coalition in weighted threshold system
assumptions: Weighted threshold rule and Boolean representation
statement_summary: Minimal winning coalitions are the prime implicants/minimal true coalitions of the threshold Boolean function; deleting a pivotal member makes the coalition losing.
limitations: Covers low-density weighted quota only; no independent continuous-state persistence filter.
notes: Subsumes weighted part, immediate-deletion logic and pivotality in P4.

theorem_label: convex/concave effective reproduction number under vector intervention
matrix_structure: next-generation matrix/operator multiplied by intervention function/vector
assumptions: Positive operator structure and source hypotheses
statement_summary: Provides sufficient conditions under which effective reproduction number is convex or concave as intervention/vaccination strategy varies and studies invariance properties.
limitations: Spectral persistence quantity, not max-over-density Allee viability; no low-density-failure boundary or coalition filter.
notes: Strong adjacent population-mathematics threat to broad novelty of vector mechanism-space convex geometry.

matrix_structure: vaccination strategy and effective reproduction number
assumptions: Source optimization framework and reducibility assumptions
statement_summary: Derives optimal vaccination/eradication properties and sufficient conditions under which scaling an optimal strategy remains optimal.
limitations: Does not produce two distinct low-density and global-persistence boundaries or an intermediate Allee phase.
